title: Indonesian Multimodal Emotion Recognition via Auxiliary-Enhanced LLM Adaptation

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating multimodal emotion recognition performance on a newly created benchmark (IndoMER) for an underrepresented language (Indonesian) to counteract the English-centric focus of existing models, along with cross-lingual evaluations on a Chinese dataset (CH-SIMS).

Measuring the model's ability to handle cross-modal inconsistencies caused by specific cultural communication norms (e.g., Indonesian cultural values like 'Rukun' and 'Sopan Santun' that encourage neutral or indirect text while conveying true emotion through prosody or facial expressions).

Evaluating fine-grained, class-wise F1 scores on long-tailed emotion distributions to measure how well the model avoids standard training biases toward majority classes (neutral, happiness) and recovers performance on rare minority classes (fear, disgust).
